thread:
alex_m: Quick question — we need to settle how QoS tags map to billing for hosted/dedicated/private. Current ambiguity: if a request falls back from Dedicated -> Hosted, who gets charged and how do we preserve the cost attribution?

jamie: Good call. Right now tokens are billed to the tenant regardless of hosting mode, but infra-level costs (what we report internally) get split. Problem is chargeback for customers who commit to Dedicated.

maria-r: We should add a persisted charge-context in the request envelope. Something like: `x-cost-center: <id>` + `x-qos-class: gold|silver|eco` so when we fallback we still attribute to the right contract.

devon: Are we sure that covers prepaid Dedicated contracts? Some Dedicated customers expect no extra per-token fees inside their pool. If we route to Hosted as a fallback we either: 1) honor the Dedicated billing terms (we invoice Redwood and absorb cost), or 2) pass-through and bill token usage per hosted pricing to that tenant. Both have implications.

alex_m: Right. Options: (A) preserve contractual semantics — mark request as "dedicated-committed" and our accounting offsets internal cost; (B) bill actual token usage on fallback and notify tenant (they accept potential overage).

jamie: Option A reduces surprises for customers but increases Redwood's exposure on fallbacks. We need telemetry to estimate how often/how expensive these fallbacks are to justify buffers.

maria-r: Implementation detail: we can propagate a `billing_hint` blob in the control plane: `{"mode":"dedicated","commit_id":"c-123","qos":"gold","attribution":"team-foo"}`. Minimal addition to API surface.

devon: Careful: `billing_hint` must be authenticated and signed by the control plane so Hosted cannot be tricked into free runs. Also need TTL — you can't reuse an old commit id.

ops-bot: deploy: Added a small feature flag `billing.hint.enabled` to staging.

jamie: Security piece okay. Another edge: private deployments (VPC/on-prem) — their analytics and billing live in their control plane. If they use our fallback mesh to Hosted (rare but allowed for cloud burst), double-accounting risk emerges.

maria-r: For private mode we require an explicit `burst_policy` with approved cost-center mapping. If the private control plane triggers Hosted fallback we attach an `origin: private-<org>` and the billing bridge will exchange settlement via monthly invoice.

alex_m: Also need to think about QoS -> scheduling. `qos=gold` should get priority in Dedicated even if it hits Hosted fallback; that affects routing and cost.

devon: That implies we must propagate QoS through the routing plane, across regions and modes, and maintain ordering guarantees for priority queues. Implementation complexity: continuous batching + prioritized preemption interacts weirdly.

jamie: Tradeoffs: adding strict priority increases tail latency variability for lower classes and complicates bin-packing across GPU pools. But it keeps customer SLAs honest.

maria-r: Propose a concrete API: headers plus a signed `billing_hint`. Example header block to include in docs:

```
X-RW-Cost-Center: team-foo
X-RW-QoS: gold
X-RW-Billing-Hint: eyJtb2RlIjoiZGVkaWNhdGVkIiwiY29tbWl0X2lkIjoiYy0xMjMiLCJ0dGwiOjE2NzcxM30=  # base64(signed json)
```

alex_m: Nice. We also need a runtime fallback policy enumerating behavior: `fallback: {action: preserve_contract | bill_hosted | reject}`. Default should be `preserve_contract` for commercial customers but expose `bill_hosted` for cost-conscious customers.

devon: Metrics to track: fallback_rate by tenant, fallback_cost_per_token, avg-queued-time-by-qos, evictions-triggered-by-qos. Need these surfaced in Console with alerting for high fallback burn.

jamie: Agree. Also legal/compliance check: private/on-prem customers may prohibit exporting usage data to Hosted. So fallback must be opt-in on private setups and disabled by default.

maria-r: Operational question: if we honor Dedicated commitment when fallbacking to Hosted, we need an internal ledger entry: debit Redwood cost center X, credit contract commit bucket Y. We should capture this in `billing-reconciler` as line-items.

alex_m: OK action items: 1) Add header spec and signed billing_hint proto (maria & devon) 2) Runtime: add `fallback.action` enum and make it configurable per tenant (jamie) 3) Console: show fallback metrics + alerting (product) 4) Billing: implement internal ledger flow for preserved-contract fallbacks (finance/billing) 5) Privacy: default fallback off for Private (maria & security)

devon: I'll prototype header signing and TTL logic. Will push a tiny RFC with sample proto and threat model.

maria-r: I'll draft the API docs and a short migration guide for Dedicated customers explaining the two fallback billing behaviors.

jamie: Great. Can we consider adding a daily quota cap on fallback consumption per tenant to avoid surprise huge bills Redwood would take on?

alex_m: Good idea — add `fallback_budget` (tokens per day) to tenant config; if exceeded, fallback behavior moves to `reject` or `bill_hosted` depending on tenant preference.

devon: Noted. I'll add that to the prototype.

alex_m: Thanks all. If no objections I'll open a follow-up RFC with the header proto + runtime behavior tomorrow. :thumbsup:
